title: Homeostasis; The human nervous system
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.5.2-c04 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.2-c09 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.2-c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; 4.5.1-c02 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.5.1-q01, 4.5.2-q01, 4.5.1-q02, 4.5.2-q02, 4.5.1-q03, 4.5.2-q03, 4.5.2-q04, 4.5.2-q05, 4.5.2-q06.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Effector
items.clue: A structure that brings about the response.

items.label: receptor
items.clue: A cell that detects a stimulus, which is a change in the environment.

questions.stem: During exercise a person's body temperature rises above its optimum level. Why does the body respond to bring the temperature back down?

options.text: To make the person feel comfortable when hot
To keep optimum conditions for enzyme action
To stop the internal conditions from changing
To let the receptors bring about the cooling

questions.explanation: Homeostasis maintains optimal conditions for enzyme action and all cell functions, so a temperature above the optimum is corrected.

questions.stem: A single neurone carries impulses from a receptor in the toe to the spinal cord. Which statement best explains how this structure is adapted to its function?

options.text: It is long, so impulses reach the CNS quickly.
It detects the stimulus and causes the response.
It is part of the central nervous system.
It carries the impulse without using the CNS.

questions.explanation: Information from receptors passes along cells (neurones) as electrical impulses to the central nervous system, so one long cell carries the impulse the whole way to the spinal cord without delay.

questions.stem: The pancreas releases a hormone that lowers a high blood glucose concentration. Which statement about this control system is correct?

options.text: A nervous response restores the optimum level
A chemical response prevents the level changing
A chemical response restores the optimum level
A receptor response restores the optimum level

questions.explanation: Automatic control systems may involve nervous responses or chemical responses; a hormone released by the pancreas is a chemical response, and the optimum blood glucose concentration is restored.

questions.stem: Effectors in the human body may be:

options.text: muscles contracting or glands secreting
receptors detecting light and sound levels
skeletal muscles moving bones at a joint
neurones carrying impulses into the brain

questions.explanation: The CNS coordinates the response of effectors, which may be muscles contracting or glands secreting hormones.

questions.stem: A person becomes cold and begins to shiver. Which structure is acting as the effector in this control system?

options.text: the muscles that contract to make the body shiver
the receptors that detect the fall in temperature
the brain that processes information from receptors
the nerves that carry impulses through the body

questions.explanation: Effectors are muscles or glands which bring about responses which restore optimum levels; here muscles contract to produce shivering.

questions.stem: In a reflex arc, what is the function of the relay neurone?

options.text: It carries the impulse to the conscious brain.
It links the sensory neurone to the motor neurone.
It carries the electrical impulse across the synapse.
It carries the impulse from the skin without the CNS.

questions.explanation: In a reflex arc the sensory neurone passes the impulse across a synapse to a relay neurone in the CNS, which passes it on to the motor neurone that carries the impulse to the effector.

questions.stem: Why is a reflex action important when a person touches a very hot object?

options.text: It gives the person time to decide how to act.
It keeps the impulse out of the nervous system.
It is automatic and rapid, so injury is reduced.
It lets the receptor make the response itself.

questions.explanation: Reflex actions are automatic and rapid; the hand is moved away from the stimulus before the conscious part of the brain is involved, which limits the damage done.

questions.stem: A table shows one student's mean reaction time in three trials: trial 1, 0.28 s; trial 2, 0.24 s; trial 3, 0.21 s. What do these data show?

options.text: The reaction time fell across the trials.
The reaction time rose across the trials.
The student reacted more slowly each time.
The results apply to other students too.

questions.explanation: Reading the values in order from the table shows a decrease from 0.28 s to 0.21 s, which is the pattern the data support.

questions.stem: Four students have mean reaction times of 0.15 s, 0.22 s, 0.28 s and 0.31 s. These values are drawn as a bar chart. Which statement about the chart is correct?

options.text: The tallest bar is the fastest time.
The shortest bar is the slowest time.
The tallest bar is the 0.31 s time.
Each bar stands for the whole group.

questions.explanation: Translating the numbers into graphical form, bar height is proportional to reaction time, so the largest value, 0.31 s, gives the tallest bar.
